title: Client socket-close protocol, resumable slices, and soft-drop cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Production telemetry in Q1 uncovered a class of failures where client sockets close mid-generation (mobile app backgrounding, flaky proxies, or abrupt network handoffs). Current heuristics either retain large partial KV caches indefinitely or aggressively drop work, causing customer-visible hallucinations, duplicate tokens, or wasted GPU cycles. This ticket introduces a formal socket-close protocol plus a resumable-slices abstraction and a "soft-drop" cleanup policy to balance correctness, cost, and latency.

Goals:
- Define a minimal wire-level handshake and server-side epoch semantics for abrupt client disconnects.
- Implement resumable slices (bounded partial-generation checkpoints) that can be reattached by returning clients or retired safely after TTL.
- Introduce soft-drop cleanup: allow graceful eviction of partial work with a short quiesce window to enable fast reclamation under load while minimizing correctness regressions.

Non-goals: full migration of legacy SDKs in this ticket (compat shims will be added separately), or changes to persistent storage layer beyond checkpoint metadata and eviction markers.
acceptance_criteria: Wire protocol: server accepts a socket-close frame (close_hint) that optionally carries the resume_token and last_known_epoch; if absent, server will treat as ephemeral disconnect
Resumable slices implemented: server writes slice metadata (slice_id, epoch, prefix_kv_hash, token_offset) to lightweight checkpoint store within 10ms write path
Soft-drop TTL policy: default quiesce window = 45s; under memory pressure, soft-drop policy allows immediate soft-invalidations followed by background compaction within 5m
Safety: no resumed client can observe duplicate token emissions or token order regressions for resumed slices in 99.99% of tests
Cost: partial checkpointing should not increase median token CPU overhead by >3% on p4d test rig
Metrics: new metrics export and dashboard validated (slice_created, slice_resumed, slice_evicted_softdrop, resume_conflict_count) and alerts wired for resume_conflict_count > 1/day for a customer
Compatibility: legacy SDKs without close_hint fallback to current best-effort behavior (no silent failures) and log a warning client-side
implementation_notes: Server: add frame handler for CLOSE_HINT (HTTP/2 custom frame or gRPC trailer key). CLOSE_HINT carries: resume_token (opaque), epoch_id (int), slice_summary (kv_hash, token_offset)

Checkpoint store: bounded in-memory metadata with optional persistence to local SSD index; metadata size per slice < 1KB. Fast path: memtable append; background worker persists/compacts to local index blobstore

Epoch lease: when CLOSE_HINT received server allocates ephemeral epoch lease (lease_ttl=60s). If client reconnects with same resume_token within lease_ttl, allow resume. If lease expired, reject resume and mark slice for soft-drop
Resume merge: attempt fuzzy merge of cached KV prefixes using prefix_kv_hash to verify compatibility; if mismatch, escalate to resume_conflict_count and prefer replay from last safe token offset

Soft-drop policy: two-step eviction: (1) soft-invalidated - mark slice inaccessible for resumption but keep cached data for background compaction (soft window 5m) ; (2) hard-evicted - free memory and delete metadata after compaction

Backpressure integration: when server memory pressure or batch queue depth exceeds thresholds, prefer soft-drop of oldest slices with least recent heartbeat. Implement priority boost for enterprise tenants tagged as 'dedicated'
Compatibility layer: SDKs will get an opt-in 'close_and_resume' flag; older clients that send no CLOSE_HINT get a short default lease (10s) on server to avoid state accumulation
Observability: emit structured events with correlation_id, client_sdk_version, region, tenant_id for every slice lifecycle transition
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate: runtime feature 'resumable_slices_v1' default off
Canary: enable feature for internal-staging, then 5% of Hosted API traffic for non-critical tenants for 48h
Monitor: watch resume_conflict_count, slice_evicted_softdrop, memory_pressure_evictions. Rollback on >5% increase in client 5xx or >20% increase in median latency for streaming endpoints
Gradual: after canary success, increase to 25% for 72h, then 100% for non-enterprise. Dedicated clusters will get admin toggle; Private customers can opt-in via upgrade guide
SDKs: publish SDK opt-in flag and RFC doc; include migration checklist for mobile/web teams to add close_and_resume on backgrounding hooks
metrics: stream.slice_created: counter by region, tenant, model
stream.slice_resumed: counter by resume_result (success, conflict, expired)
stream.slice_evicted_softdrop: counter and gauge for bytes reclaimed
stream.resume_latency_ms: histogram (time between reconnect and resume complete)
infra.memory_pressure_evictions: gauge correlated with slice evictions
dependencies: runtime/pull/12345 - PR adding CloseHint frame handler
test_plan: Unit: frame encoding/decoding tests for CLOSE_HINT including malformed tokens
Integration: simulate client abrupt socket close then reconnect within lease_ttl with resumed tokens; validate token order and no duplicates
Chaos: randomized network flakiness test for 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with soft-drop enabled; assert memory growth bounded
Perf: measure p99 latency and token CPU overhead on p4d with load test harness before/after enabling resumable slices
Compatibility: test with legacy SDK versions (v0.9.x) to ensure default behavior unchanged
